newsitem.title: USA: Boeing has agreements for 747 stretch.
newsitem.headline: Boeing has agreements for 747 stretch.

text.p: Thai Airways and Malaysia Airline System have agreed to purchase stretch versions of Boeing Co's 747 jumbo jet if and when the program is launched, officials of the manufacturer said.

At a media briefing Boeing executives confirmed reports published last month that the two Asian airlines have signed purchase agreements. The executives did not disclose the size of the potential deals but said there were not yet sufficient orders to justify launching the program.
"It's going to take another six months or less for us to make a decision to launch it," John Roundhill, director of engineering for the program, said late Saturday.
If the program is launched in the next six months, the first delivery of an enlarged 747 would be in the last half of 2001, he said.

He said airlines were moving cautiously before deciding whether to buy the proposed new jet but said a competing offer from Airbus Industrie, which is proposing an all-new super-jumbo jet dubbed the A3XX, was not having any effect on potential customers.
Instead he said airlines were waiting to see what kind of engine would be offered by a new venture of General Electric Co and United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney unit.
Roundhill said the Boeing 747-600X being offered, which would seat about 100 more passengers than the current 747-400, carried a list price of slightly less than $200 million.
A second version, known as the 747-500X, would carry fewer passengers but have a longer range and likely would be launched after the -600x, he said.
